Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 108, verse 1:

Surat al-Kawthar (Sūrat al-Kawthar)[[In "A" the surah is titled: Surat Inna A'taynāka.]]

Makkiyyah (Meccan)[[Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Surat (Inna A'taynaka al-Kawthar) was revealed in Mecca." See al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/646.]] In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar.﴾ Ismail ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Huladi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad Ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us: 'Ali ibn Mushhir informed us, from al-Mukhtar — that is, Ibn Fulful — from Anas, who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among us one day, he dozed off briefly, then raised his head smiling. We said: 'What made you laugh, Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'A surah has just been revealed to me.' Then he recited: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Indeed, the one who hates you is the one cut off.﴾' Then he said: 'Do you know what al-Kawthar is?' We said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'It is a river which my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, promised me. On it is abundant good. It is a basin to which my nation will come on the Day of Resurrection; its vessels are as numerous as the stars. A servant among them will be pulled back, and I will say: "My Lord, he is from me." He will say: "You do not know what he introduced after you."'"[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Salah, chapter on the proof of those who say that the basmalah is a verse at the beginning of every surah except Bara'ah, no. (400): 1/300.]]

'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: 'Amr ibn Muhammad informed us: Hushaym informed us: Abu Bishr and 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Kawthar" is the abundant good which Allah gave him. Abu Bishr said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Some people claim that it is a river in Paradise." Sa'id said: "The river in Paradise is part of the good which Allah gave him."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Tafsir of Surat al-Kawthar: 8/731, and in al-Riqaq; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/167-168.]]

al-Hasan said: It is the Great Qur'an.

'Ikrimah said: Prophethood and the Book.[[Narrated by Hannad in al-Zuhd: 1/221, and Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 11/508, and al-Tabari: 30/322, and its chain is sound.]]

The lexicographers said: al-Kawthar is on the pattern fawʿal (fawʿal) [from kathrah (abundance), like Nawfal: fawʿal][[The words in brackets are omitted from "B".]] from al-nafl (surplus), and the Arabs call everything that is abundant in number or in quantity and worth "kawthar." [abundant in number or][[The words in brackets are omitted from "A".]] It is well known that it is a river in Paradise which Allah gave to His Messenger (ﷺ), as has come in the hadith:

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tays-funi informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Jawhari informed us: Ahmad ibn [ʿAli][[In "A" it reads "Abd Allah"; the correct form is what is established here.]] al-Kushmihani informed us: 'Ali ibn Hujr informed us: Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us: Humayd informed us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I entered Paradise and behold, there was a river whose whiteness [of] [[omitted from "A"]] milk flows, sweeter than honey, and its two banks are tents of pearls. I struck with my hand and its soil was musk, pungent. I said to Jibril: 'What is this?' He said: 'It is al-Kawthar which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave you.'"[[A sound hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/103, 115, through Humayd from Anas; and Hannad in al-Zuhd: 1/211; and al-Nasa'i in al-Tafsir: 2/559; and al-Tabari: 30/323-324; and Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 13/147; and al-Ajurri in al-Shari'ah p. 396; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/170. Al-Bukhari narrated it through Qatadah from Anas in similar wording, in al-Riqaq, chapter on the basin: 11/464.]]

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi informed us: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa al-Salt informed us: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj informed us: Muhammad ibn Fudayl informed us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise; its banks are gold, its course is over pearls and rubies, its soil is more fragrant than musk, and whiter than snow."[[A sound hadith narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Riqaq: 2/337; and al-Tirmidhi in al-Tafsir, Tafsir of Surat al-Kawthar: 9/294, who said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith"; and Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, no. (4334): 2/1450, through several routes from 'Ata' ibn Abi al-Sa'ib from Muharib ibn Dithar from Ibn 'Umar; and al-Darimi in al-Riqaq, chapter on al-Kawthar: 2/338; and al-Hakim: 3/171; and Hannad in al-Zuhd: 1/208; and Imam Ahmad: 2/67, 158; and al-Tabari: 30/324; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/168-169. Shaykh al-Arna'ut said: ... and 'Ata' heard from Muharib before the confusion (ikhtilat). See also Fath al-Bari: 8/732, and Hannad's al-Zuhd: 1/209 with the editor's commentary.]]

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam informed us: Nafi' [ibn 'Umar, from][[omitted from "B"]] Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My basin is a month's journey; its water is whiter than milk, its fragrance is more pleasant than musk, and its cups are like the stars of the sky. Whoever drinks from it will never thirst again."[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Riqaq, chapter on the basin: 11/463; and Muslim in al-Fada'il, chapter on affirming the basin of our Prophet (ﷺ), no. (2292): 4/1794; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/168.]]

Abu Sa'id 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us: my grandfather 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzaz informed us: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-'Adhafiri informed us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "[I am at the rear of my basin] [[The words in brackets are omitted from "A"; 'uqr al-hawd means its rear part.]] I drive people away from it, as one drives away the people of Yemen. I strike them with my staff until they scatter from it. And indeed it gushes [with] [[i.e., pours water in continuous streams.]] two spouts from Paradise in it, one of silver and the other of gold, its length being the distance between Busra and San'a', or between Aylah and Makkah, or from this place of mine to 'Uman."[[Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 11/406; and Muslim in al-Fada'il, chapter on affirming the basin of our Prophet (ﷺ) and its attributes, no. (2301): 4/1799; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/169.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 108, verse 2:

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Some people used to pray to other than God and sacrifice to other than God, so God commanded His Prophet ﷺ to pray and sacrifice to God, Mighty and Majestic [[See al-Tabari: 30/327.]].

ʿIkrimah, ʿAta' and Qatadah said: "So pray to your Lord" means the ʿId prayer on the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), "and sacrifice" means your nusuk (the sacrificial offering).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: "So pray" means the obligatory prayers at Jam' (Muzdalifah), and "sacrifice the camels" means at Mina [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/651.]].

It is narrated from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "So pray to your Lord and sacrifice" — he said: placing the right hand upon the left during prayer at the time of sacrifice [[This is also narrated from ʿAli, as is found in al-Tabari: 30/325, and from al-Sha'bi something similar, but it is not authentic. al-Tabari narrated the reports in 30/325–328 and then said: "The most correct of these opinions in my view is the opinion of the one who said: the meaning of that is: make your entire prayer purely for your Lord, apart from whatever else is a rival or a deity, and likewise make your sacrifice for Him alone, apart from the idols, in gratitude for the honour and the good He has bestowed upon you, which has no equal, and His giving you al-Kawthar." Ibn Kathir approved this in his tafsir: 4/560.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 108, verse 3:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your enemy﴾ (shani'ak), meaning your foe [[Al-Bukhari cited it in suspended form (ta'liq) from Ibn 'Abbas in al-Fath (8/731), and Ibn Mardawayh connected it with a full chain.]] and your hater, ﴿he is the one cut off﴾ (al-abtar). The abtar is the one who is least, the most humiliated, whose line is cut off. [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (4/560): "They imagined, in their ignorance, that when his sons died his remembrance would be cut off and he would die. Far be it, no indeed! Rather, God has preserved his remembrance upon the heads of witnesses, and has made his law obligatory upon the necks of servants, enduring through the ages, until the Day of Gathering and Resurrection, may God's blessings and peace be upon him continually until the Day of Calling."]]

It was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi. The reason was that he saw the Prophet ﷺ coming out of the mosque's gate while he was entering, so the two met at the gate of Banu Sahm and conversed, while some of the chieftains of Quraysh were sitting in the mosques. When al-'As entered, they said to him: "Who was the one you were talking with?" He said: "That abtar," meaning the Prophet ﷺ, for a son of the Messenger of God ﷺ by Khadija (may God be pleased with her) had died. [[Narrated by al-Tabari (30/329) and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 541. See also Ibn Kathir (4/560) and al-Durr al-Manthur (8/653). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (8/732): "The transmitters differed in identifying the mentioned shani'. It was said: he is al-'As ibn Wa'il; it was said: he is Abu Jahl; and it was said: 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt." See also Ibn Kathir (4/560), who mentioned other opinions.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from Yazid ibn Ruman, who said: Whenever the Messenger of God ﷺ was mentioned, al-'As ibn Wa'il would say: "Leave him, for he is an abtar man with no offspring; when he dies, his remembrance will be cut off." So God the Exalted revealed this surah. [[Narrated by Ibn Ishaq without a chain (mursal), in Ibn Hisham's Sira, 1/393. See also al-Tabari (30/329), Ibn Kathir (4/560), al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul pp. 541–542, and al-Durr al-Manthur (8/652).]]

Ikrima said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: It was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and a group of Quraysh. The reason was that when Ka'b came to Makka, Quraysh said to him: "We are the people of the water-drawing (al-siqaya) and the custodianship (al-sadana), and you are the chief of the people of Madina. Are we better, or is this cut-off stump (al-sunbur al-munbatir) of his people?" He said: "Rather, you are better than him." So God revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who believe in idols and false deities?﴾ [al-Nisa': 51], and it was revealed concerning those who said he was abtar: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, that is, cut off from every good. [[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Tafsir (2/560), al-Tabari (30/330), and Ibn Hibban, who authenticated it, no. 1731 in Mawarid al-Zam'an. Ibn Kathir (4/560) cited it from al-Bazzar (without the mention of the verse of Surat al-Nisa') and authenticated its chain. al-Suyuti in al-Durr (8/652) added its attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh.]]
